words.childMeaning: Based on ideas rather than on practical experience.
practiceSentences: The plan is theoretical until somebody tries it.
Is this a theoretical or a practical problem?
Theoretical knowledge needs testing in the world.
She gave a theoretical answer, which did not help.
A theoretical risk can still be worth planning for.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: One of a kind; very special.
practiceSentences: Every genre has its own unique features, which is how readers tell them apart.
Every snowflake has a unique pattern that no other snowflake shares.
What makes your fingerprint unique compared with everyone else's?
"Each of you has a unique talent," our head teacher reminded the assembly.
I keep a unique spiral shell on my shelf that I found on holiday.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: True or shared everywhere, by everyone.
practiceSentences: Grief is a universal human experience.
Is that rule universal, or local to us?
The story's appeal is universal.
Some symbols are close to universal.
A universal claim is the hardest kind to prove.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: Not expected to happen or be true; improbable.
practiceSentences: It seems unlikely that the well will fill again before winter.
Is it unlikely that Zara remembers every word she has heard?
What an unlikely ending to such a strange story!
Jamal thought rain was unlikely, but the sky soon turned grey.
Storytellers add unlikely details until the tale outgrows the truth.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: Well founded, and able to stand up to examination.
practiceSentences: That is a valid objection and deserves an answer.
Is the argument still valid without this evidence?
A valid ticket must show today's date.
Her reasoning was valid even where I disagreed.
One weak step makes the whole proof less valid.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: Extremely large in size or amount.
practiceSentences: A vast plain stretched to the horizon.
How vast is the desert to the north?
There is a vast difference between the two drafts.
The library holds a vast collection of maps.
Vast is a stronger word than big, and rarer.

words.group: Words: kinds of writing and how they read
words.childMeaning: Absolutely necessary for something to work or survive.
practiceSentences: Water is vital to every living thing.
Why is this step vital to the argument?
A vital piece of evidence was missing.
Sleep is vital, not a luxury.
The vital question is who benefits.

words.childMeaning: Although; even though.
practiceSentences: The plan worked, albeit more slowly than hoped.
She agreed, albeit with some hesitation.
It was a fair result, albeit a disappointing one.
He finished the race, albeit in last place.
The essay is good, albeit a little long.

words.childMeaning: Without being affected by something else.
practiceSentences: She went on regardless of the rain.
Will the match go ahead regardless?
Regardless of the cost, the repair must happen.
He spoke his mind regardless of who was listening.
The rule applies regardless of age.

words.childMeaning: The number 40, which is four groups of ten ones.
practiceSentences: Forty birds landed on the roof beside the market.
Can you write forty in words and in numerals?
"We still need forty more beans," said Sami quietly.
My grandmother gave me forty tiny buttons to count.
Leo jumped forty centimetres further than yesterday.

words.childMeaning: Enough for what is needed.
practiceSentences: Two litres will be sufficient for the whole class.
Is one sample sufficient to draw a conclusion?
We had sufficient time, but used it badly.
Sufficient evidence is not the same as proof.
A short note was sufficient to explain the change.

words.childMeaning: Complete and careful, leaving nothing out.
practiceSentences: She made a thorough check of every measurement.
How thorough was the search?
A thorough answer takes longer to write.
The report was thorough but far too long.
Be thorough with the first step and the rest is easier.

words.childMeaning: A firm promise that something will happen or be done.
practiceSentences: The shop gives a two-year guarantee on the kettle.
Can you guarantee the results will be the same?
Practice is no guarantee of success, but it helps.
There is no guarantee that the rain will hold off.
She would not guarantee a figure she had not checked.

words.childMeaning: Single and separate, rather than part of a group.
practiceSentences: Each individual answer was marked separately.
What individual difference did you notice?
An individual result tells you less than the set.
She kept an individual record for every plant.
The average hides what each individual did.

words.childMeaning: Maths that uses letters to stand for unknown numbers.
practiceSentences: In algebra, x can stand for any number.
Why does algebra use letters instead of numbers?
Algebra lets you write a rule that always works.
She solved the algebra question in two lines.
Algebra begins where arithmetic stops.

words.childMeaning: A chart of bars showing how often values fall in each range.
practiceSentences: The histogram shows how many pupils scored in each band.
What does this histogram tell you about the class?
A histogram has no gaps between its bars.
She drew a histogram of the daily rainfall.
A histogram groups values; a bar chart names them.

words.childMeaning: A chart that uses pictures to stand for numbers.
practiceSentences: Each book on the pictogram stands for five readers.
What does one symbol represent on this pictogram?
A pictogram needs a key or it means nothing.
The class made a pictogram of favourite fruits.
Half a picture on a pictogram means half the value.

words.childMeaning: The distance all the way around a circle.
practiceSentences: Measure the circumference with a piece of string.
What is the circumference of this wheel?
The circumference grows as the radius grows.
She calculated the circumference from the diameter.
A circle's circumference is a little over three diameters.

words.childMeaning: A number written with a point, such as 3.75.
practiceSentences: Write the fraction as a decimal.
Which decimal is larger, 0.7 or 0.65?
A decimal point separates whole from part.
Money is written as a decimal in most countries.
She rounded the decimal to two places.

words.childMeaning: A statement that two amounts are equal.
practiceSentences: An equation always has an equals sign.
Can you solve this equation for x?
Both sides of an equation must balance.
She checked the equation by putting the answer back.
One equation cannot give you two unknowns.

words.childMeaning: A number that divides exactly into another number.
practiceSentences: Three is a factor of twelve.
Which factors does eighteen have?
Every number has one and itself as factors.
List the factors before you look for a common one.
A prime number has exactly two factors.

words.childMeaning: A pattern of evenly spaced lines crossing each other.
practiceSentences: Plot the point on the grid using both coordinates.
How many squares does this grid have?
A map grid lets two people name the same spot.
She drew the shape on squared grid paper.
The grid reference gives an exact location.

words.childMeaning: A statement that two amounts are not equal.
practiceSentences: The inequality says x is greater than five.
Which sign shows this inequality?
An inequality has a range of answers, not one.
She graphed the inequality on a number line.
Reversing the sides reverses the inequality.

words.childMeaning: A whole number, with no fraction or decimal part.
practiceSentences: Seven is an integer; seven and a half is not.
Which of these values is an integer?
Integers include negative whole numbers too.
Round the answer to the nearest integer.
Zero is an integer, and it is neither positive nor negative.

words.childMeaning: The average found by adding values and dividing by how many.
practiceSentences: Add the five scores and divide to find the mean.
What is the mean of these numbers?
The mean can be pulled about by one extreme value.
The mean and the median are not the same thing.
She reported the mean rainfall for each month.

words.childMeaning: The middle value when the numbers are put in order.
practiceSentences: Put the values in order, then find the median.
What is the median of this set?
The median ignores how extreme the ends are.
With an even number of values, the median is the middle two averaged.
The median often describes a group better than the mean.

words.childMeaning: A number you get by multiplying another number.
practiceSentences: Twelve is a multiple of three.
Which multiples of four are under thirty?
Every number is a multiple of one.
A common multiple appears in both times tables.
Factors divide into it; multiples come out of it.

words.childMeaning: A part of a whole expressed out of a hundred.
practiceSentences: What percentage of the class walks to school?
How do you turn a fraction into a percentage?
A percentage always compares to one hundred.
The percentage rose from twelve to twenty.
Fifty per cent is a percentage and also a half.

words.childMeaning: A flat shape with three or more straight sides.
practiceSentences: A triangle is the simplest polygon.
How many sides does this polygon have?
A circle is not a polygon.
A regular polygon has equal sides and angles.
She named every polygon on the sheet.

words.childMeaning: A number divisible only by itself and one.
practiceSentences: Seven is a prime number.
Which prime numbers are under twenty?
A prime has exactly two factors.
One is not prime, because it has only one factor.
Every whole number breaks down into primes.

words.childMeaning: How likely something is to happen.
practiceSentences: The probability of heads is one half.
What is the probability of rain today?
A probability of zero means it cannot happen.
Probability is written as a fraction or a decimal.
High probability is not the same as certainty.

words.childMeaning: The answer you get when you divide one number by another.
practiceSentences: Twenty divided by four gives a quotient of five.
What is the quotient in this division?
The quotient may have a remainder beside it.
Write the quotient above the division line.
A larger divisor makes a smaller quotient.

words.childMeaning: A comparison showing how much of one thing there is to another.
practiceSentences: The ratio of boys to girls is three to four.
What ratio of water to flour does the recipe need?
A ratio can be simplified like a fraction.
The map uses a ratio of one to fifty thousand.
Two to one is a ratio, not a fraction.

words.childMeaning: Numbers collected about something, and the study of them.
practiceSentences: The statistics show a steady rise in readers.
What do these statistics actually prove?
Statistics can mislead if the sample is small.
She gathered statistics on journeys to school.
Good statistics need an honest question first.

words.childMeaning: Something that can change, or a letter standing for it.
practiceSentences: In this equation, x is the variable.
Which variable did you change in the test?
Keep every other variable the same.
A variable can take many values.
Temperature was the variable they measured.

words.childMeaning: An angle smaller than a right angle.
practiceSentences: An acute angle is less than ninety degrees.
Which of these angles is acute?
A triangle can have three acute angles.
The roof met the wall at an acute angle.
Acute is sharp; obtuse is blunt.

words.childMeaning: An angle larger than a right angle but less than a straight one.
practiceSentences: An obtuse angle is more than ninety degrees.
Is this angle obtuse or reflex?
A triangle can have only one obtuse angle.
The two roads met at an obtuse angle.
Obtuse angles look open rather than sharp.

words.childMeaning: Lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
practiceSentences: Railway lines are parallel to each other.
Which sides of this shape are parallel?
Parallel lines never meet, however far you draw them.
She marked the parallel sides with arrows.
A square has two pairs of parallel sides.

words.childMeaning: At a right angle to something else.
practiceSentences: The post stands perpendicular to the ground.
Which line is perpendicular to this one?
Perpendicular lines cross at ninety degrees.
She checked the wall was perpendicular with a square.
Perpendicular and parallel are opposites here.

words.childMeaning: The changing of something from one form into another.
practiceSentences: The conversion of the warehouse into a clinic took a year.
How difficult is the conversion of sunlight into electricity?
Work out the conversion from metres into centimetres.
The conversion of the school hall gave families shelter.
A conversion table saves you the arithmetic.

words.childMeaning: A line on a map running from the North Pole to the South.
practiceSentences: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich.
Which meridian runs closest to your town?
Every meridian is a line of longitude.
Meridians meet at both poles.
Time zones are measured from the prime meridian.

words.childMeaning: The movement of people or animals from one place to another.
practiceSentences: The birds begin their migration in autumn.
What causes the migration of these fish?
Migration follows food and warmth.
The map traces the migration route year by year.
Drought can force migration from a whole region.

words.childMeaning: A number with more than two factors.
practiceSentences: Nine is a composite number.
Which of these numbers is composite?
Every whole number above one is prime or composite.
A composite number can be broken into factors.
Four is the smallest composite number.

words.childMeaning: The number you are dividing by.
practiceSentences: In twenty divided by five, five is the divisor.
Which divisor gives a whole answer?
A larger divisor gives a smaller quotient.
The remainder must be less than the divisor.
Zero can never be a divisor.

words.childMeaning: The number being divided.
practiceSentences: In twenty divided by five, twenty is the dividend.
What is the dividend in this calculation?
The dividend sits inside the division sign.
Divide the dividend by the divisor.
A larger dividend gives a larger quotient.

words.group: Words that link by means or place
words.childMeaning: By that means; as a result of that.
practiceSentences: She checked her working, thereby catching the error.
They planted trees, thereby slowing the erosion.
He arrived early, thereby getting the best seat.
The bridge reopened, thereby shortening every journey.
Round early and you thereby lose accuracy.

words.group: Words that link by means or place
words.childMeaning: By which; through which something happens.
practiceSentences: A method whereby the answer can be checked.
Is there a rule whereby exceptions are allowed?
They agreed a system whereby each class takes a turn.
The process whereby rock becomes soil is slow.
She explained the way whereby the two connect.

words.childMeaning: A job that needs long training or study.
practiceSentences: Medicine is a profession that takes years to enter.
Which profession would you choose?
She left one profession for another at forty.
Teaching is a profession, not merely a job.
Every profession has its own rules of conduct.

words.childMeaning: A place where people buy and eat meals that cooks make.
practiceSentences: The restaurant near the station serves hot rice at lunchtime.
The family restaurant serves grilled fish every Friday.
Which restaurant makes the best lamb kebabs in town?
"This restaurant is open," said Father, reading the sign.
I helped choose the restaurant for Grandmother's birthday dinner.

words.childMeaning: An organisation that makes or sells things for money.
practiceSentences: Her business sells honey from local hives.
How long has the business been trading?
A small business can grow from one good idea.
The business employs four people.
Running a business means keeping careful records.

words.childMeaning: A small group chosen to make decisions for a larger one.
practiceSentences: The committee meets on the first Monday of term.
Who sits on the school committee?
A committee decides on behalf of everyone else.
The committee voted to plant a hedge.
She was elected to the committee last year.

words.childMeaning: A person's name written by hand to show they agree.
practiceSentences: The form needs a parent's signature.
Whose signature is on the bottom of the page?
A signature is hard to copy convincingly.
She added her signature and the date.
Without a signature the letter means nothing.

words.childMeaning: A person who manages the daily running of an organisation.
practiceSentences: The administrator keeps the school records in order.
Who is the administrator for this department?
An administrator makes the place work without being seen.
She trained as an administrator after leaving school.
The administrator handles every booking.

words.childMeaning: A person whose job is to give expert advice.
practiceSentences: The council appointed a legal adviser.
Who acts as adviser to the committee?
A good adviser tells you what you would rather not hear.
She works as a careers adviser at the school.
An adviser suggests; the decision stays yours.

words.childMeaning: A person who represents their country in another country.
practiceSentences: The ambassador attended the opening of the bridge.
Which country does the ambassador represent?
An ambassador speaks for a whole nation.
She was made ambassador at the age of forty.
The ambassador's residence stands beside the park.

words.childMeaning: A person who formally asks for a job or a place.
practiceSentences: Every applicant must complete the same form.
How many applicants applied for the post?
The strongest applicant was not the loudest.
Each applicant is interviewed for twenty minutes.
An applicant should read the advertisement twice.

words.childMeaning: A person who receives help, money or an advantage.
practiceSentences: The village was the main beneficiary of the grant.
Who is the beneficiary of this scheme?
A beneficiary need not have asked for anything.
She named her sister as the beneficiary.
Every beneficiary was written to in advance.

words.childMeaning: A person who works publicly to change something.
practiceSentences: The campaigner spoke outside the town hall.
What is the campaigner asking for?
A campaigner needs patience more than volume.
She became a campaigner for safer crossings.
One campaigner started with a single letter.

words.childMeaning: A person who is not in the armed forces or the police.
practiceSentences: The airfield is closed to civilian traffic.
How many civilians live in the valley?
A civilian may not enter the base.
She returned to civilian life after ten years.
Civilian clothes felt strange after the uniform.

words.childMeaning: A person or team taking part in a contest.
practiceSentences: Each competitor wore a number on their back.
How many competitors entered this year?
The youngest competitor finished third.
A competitor may withdraw at any point.
Every competitor shook hands afterwards.

words.childMeaning: A person or firm hired to do a particular job.
practiceSentences: The contractor begins work on the roof in June.
Which contractor won the bid?
A contractor is paid for the job, not the hours.
The contractor left the site tidy each evening.
They asked three contractors for a price.

words.childMeaning: A person who gives money, work or ideas to something.
practiceSentences: Every contributor was thanked by name.
Who was the largest contributor to the fund?
A contributor need not be the loudest voice.
She is a regular contributor to the school paper.
Each contributor added one page to the book.

words.childMeaning: A person elected to serve on a local council.
practiceSentences: The councillor visited the flooded street herself.
Which councillor represents this ward?
A councillor is elected by local people.
She wrote to her councillor about the bus route.
The councillor voted against the proposal.

words.childMeaning: The person in a court case who is accused.
practiceSentences: The defendant listened without speaking.
What did the defendant say in reply?
A defendant is innocent until it is proved otherwise.
The defendant was represented by a lawyer.
Both the defendant and the witness were questioned.

words.childMeaning: A person chosen to represent a group at a meeting.
practiceSentences: Each class sent one delegate to the council.
Who is the delegate for your year group?
A delegate carries the group's view, not their own.
The delegate reported back on Friday.
Every delegate was given ten minutes to speak.

words.childMeaning: A person who is in charge of an organisation or a film.
practiceSentences: The director opened the meeting at nine.
Who is the director of the museum?
A director decides the overall direction.
The film's director rewrote the ending.
She became a director after fifteen years.

words.childMeaning: A person who leads and makes decisions for a city or region.
practiceSentences: The governor listens to the whole town before she signs any plan.
What decisions does a governor make for the region?
The governor opened the new hospital with a short speech.
"The governor promised cleaner parks," reported the newspaper.
We wrote letters to the governor about our broken playground.

words.childMeaning: An official whose job is to check that rules are followed.
practiceSentences: The inspector checked every fire door.
When does the inspector visit?
An inspector reports what is found, not what is hoped.
The health inspector gave the kitchen top marks.
She trained as a safety inspector.

words.childMeaning: A person who puts money into something to earn more later.
practiceSentences: An investor paid for the new machinery.
What does an investor expect in return?
Every investor accepts some risk.
The investor asked to see the accounts first.
A patient investor waits years for a return.

words.childMeaning: A group of people who decide a verdict in a court case.
practiceSentences: The jury listened to both sides carefully.
How many people sit on a jury?
A jury decides the facts, not the law.
The jury retired to consider its verdict.
Serving on a jury is a public duty.

words.childMeaning: A senior member of a government in charge of one area.
practiceSentences: The minister answered questions for an hour.
Which minister is responsible for schools?
A minister leads a whole department.
The minister visited the flooded district.
She was appointed minister last spring.

words.childMeaning: A person who competes or argues against you.
practiceSentences: Her opponent conceded before the final round.
Who is your opponent in the debate?
Respect an opponent and you argue better.
The two opponents shook hands afterwards.
An opponent is not an enemy.

words.childMeaning: A person who plans and arranges an event.
practiceSentences: The organiser booked the hall six months ahead.
Who is the organiser of the fair?
A good organiser is never noticed on the day.
The organisers thanked every helper.
She acts as organiser for the reading club.

words.childMeaning: A person chosen to speak or act for a group.
practiceSentences: Each class elects one representative.
Who is the representative for your year?
A representative reports back to the people who chose them.
The representative put the class's view clearly.
She served as representative for two terms.

words.childMeaning: A person who studies a subject carefully to find things out.
practiceSentences: The researcher spent two years on the study.
What is the researcher trying to find out?
A researcher records what happens, not what was hoped.
She works as a researcher at the university.
Every researcher must check their sources.

words.childMeaning: A person with deep knowledge of one particular subject.
practiceSentences: The doctor referred her to a specialist.
Which specialist should we ask?
A specialist knows one field very well indeed.
He is a specialist in old maps.
Sometimes a generalist sees what a specialist misses.

words.childMeaning: A person or firm that pays to support something.
practiceSentences: A local shop is the sponsor of the team's kit.
Who sponsors the reading challenge?
A sponsor usually expects their name to be shown.
They found a sponsor for the whole tournament.
She sponsored her cousin's walk for charity.

words.childMeaning: A person who pays taxes to the government.
practiceSentences: Every taxpayer helps fund the schools.
What does the taxpayer get in return?
A taxpayer has a right to ask how money is spent.
The road was built with taxpayers' money.
Taxpayers were asked for their views first.

words.childMeaning: A person who pays to live in a house or flat.
practiceSentences: The tenant upstairs waters the plants on the shared balcony.
Does the tenant help water the shared garden too?
The new tenant moved into the flat above the bakery.
"A good tenant keeps the house tidy," said the landlord.
My uncle is a tenant in a building near the library.

words.childMeaning: A person whose work is buying and selling goods.
practiceSentences: The trader sells cloth at the Tuesday market.
What does this trader deal in?
A trader must know what a thing is worth.
The trader lowered the price at closing time.
Traders came from three towns to the fair.

words.childMeaning: A plan for how money will be earned and spent.
practiceSentences: The class set a budget for the trip.
How much is left in the budget?
A budget is a plan, not a wish.
She kept to the budget by cutting one item.
The council publishes its budget each year.

words.childMeaning: The buying and selling of goods on a large scale.
practiceSentences: The port has been a centre of commerce for centuries.
How has commerce changed the town?
Commerce needs roads as much as it needs money.
Online commerce reached the village late.
Commerce and trade mean much the same thing.

words.childMeaning: A business that makes or sells things.
practiceSentences: The company employs thirty people.
Which company made this machine?
A company must keep proper accounts.
She started the company with one van.
The company published its results in May.

words.childMeaning: In any case; whatever else is true.
practiceSentences: It was late, but she finished the letter anyhow.
Are you coming anyhow?
The bus was full; we walked anyhow.
Anyhow, the decision has already been made.
He had no map and set off anyhow.

words.childMeaning: Anyway means despite what has just been said, or in spite of any difficulties.
practiceSentences: Amal raised her hand anyway, even though her voice shook.
Are you going to the fair anyway, Zara?
Grandma Hana felt tired, but she cooked the soup anyway.
I am not sure it will work, but let's try it anyway!
The path looked blocked, so they went round it anyway.

words.childMeaning: Someone who is very forceful or ready to fight.
A reason given to support an idea, or a disagreement between people.
practiceSentences: Sami built a strong argument using facts from the report.
Is fear really a good argument for silencing people?
Amal! Your argument convinced the whole class.
A short argument broke out over who would present first.
Choosing the wrong register weakens even the most precise argument.

A written agreement between two or more people or groups
practiceSentences: Every player signed the team contract before the first football match.
The astronauts signed a contract promising to follow every safety rule.
What happens if a builder breaks the contract with the town?
"Read the whole contract carefully before you sign anything," Father always says.
Our class wrote a homework contract, and everyone signed it in blue ink.

words.childMeaning: The money a person earns from working or selling things.
practiceSentences: Omar's income depended on how many fish he sold each day.
Does a market trader's income change with the seasons?
Their income barely covered the rent that month!
Teacher Yasmin explained how income and spending must balance.
My income dried up like a puddle in the midday sun.

words.childMeaning: Hard work, or the people who do it.
practiceSentences: Harvest labour keeps the whole village busy for weeks.
Building the barn took months of hard labour.
Why does farm labour begin before the sun rises?
"Honest labour brings its own reward," said Grandfather.
I respect the labour that brings food to our table.

words.childMeaning: A plan or rule that helps people decide what to do.
practiceSentences: Every classroom in our school follows the same policy about sharing equipment fairly.
The library's new policy lets pupils renew their books online from home.
Should our school adopt a policy about kindness in the playground?
"Our family policy is homework first, then games," said Father firmly.
The mayor explained the city's recycling policy during her visit to our class.

words.childMeaning: A regulation is an official rule made by an authority to control how something is done.
Keeping yourself and your surroundings clean in order to stay healthy.
A sickness caused by germs that can spread.
practiceSentences: Nurses wash their hands carefully so no infection passes from patient to patient.
Washing your hands before meals helps stop infection from spreading around.
How does a doctor know if a small cut has an infection?
"Keep the plaster on so the infection cannot get any worse," said the nurse.
Theo missed a whole week of school because of an ear infection.

words.childMeaning: The process plants use to make their own food from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Toxic means poisonous or extremely harmful to people, animals, or the environment.

practiceSentences: Two years earlier an earthquake had broken their town, and many families had moved away.
"My son was ill after the earthquake," the woman whispered.
Two years earlier an earthquake had shaken the whole valley.

words.childMeaning: A mountain that can erupt with hot lava, ash, and gas.
practiceSentences: Scientists watch the volcano closely for smoke and small shakes.
Hot lava poured slowly down the side of the volcano.
How long has that volcano been quiet and still?
"Our model volcano will fizz and bubble," said Adam.
I built a clay volcano for the science fair.

words.childMeaning: Willing means ready and happy to do something.
practiceSentences: Talia was willing to stay late to care for the injured animal.
Are the villagers willing to give up using snares?
Sami, thank you for being so willing to help!
The whole class seemed willing to volunteer at the reserve.
AMAL: Local families now say they are willing to build better fences.
